title: Drive
author: Daniel H. Pink
blurb: Why do we work hard? For most of the last century, organizations assumed the answer was simple: reward the behavior you want and punish the behavior you don't. Daniel Pink argues this carrot-and-stick approach is badly out of date. Drawing on decades of behavioral science, he shows that external rewards work well for simple, routine tasks but can hurt performance and creativity on complex, open-ended work. What truly drives us, he says, is a third drive: the inner desire to direct our own lives, get better at things that matter, and contribute to something larger than ourselves. Pink calls these autonomy, mastery, and purpose. He shows how companies, schools, and individuals can build around them. They start with fair baseline pay so money stops being a distraction. Then they give people the freedom and challenge to do their best work.

lessons.b: Experiments like Harry Harlow's monkeys solving puzzles for no reward, and Edward Deci's puzzle studies, revealed a third drive: we do some things simply because they are satisfying.
